slr_claim_paraphrase: Analyzing third-party libraries can produce additional valid alerts.
limitation: This is about method-level analysis coverage, not merely reporting already-produced alerts and not precision.

slr_claim_paraphrase: Whitelisting common third-party libraries prevents over-counting.
limitation: It motivates a reporting/filtering design assumption but does not identify an effect on precision.

slr_claim_paraphrase: Package-name attribution against a library list maps call sites to third-party libraries.
limitation: It supports the provenance measurement procedure, not an outcome edge.

slr_claim_paraphrase: Incomplete ground truth lowers observed precision.
limitation: Ground-truth completeness is not measured in the four final datasets.

slr_claim_paraphrase: Detection rules derived from implementation flaws can improve accuracy.
limitation: The claim concerns rule design; observed rule IDs are not randomized.

slr_claim_paraphrase: Alert-refinement algorithms can remove false positives.
limitation: The refinement is built into a tool and is not separately measured here.

slr_claim_paraphrase: Integrating external/library code can reduce scalability.
limitation: This concerns analyzing library code, not reporting third-party-library alerts, and has a different outcome.
